architecture_interpretation.current_direction: hybrid Forest architecture rather than replacing Lodgepole outright
architecture_interpretation.lodgepole: hierarchical shared structure and coarse routing

experiment.name: Forest Topology V5
experiment.purpose: Test whether Orange correlated wedges can be selected on held-out tokens without inspecting held-out residual energy.

limitations: Routing currently uses layer identity and aggregate training statistics rather than prompt-specific semantic routing.
V5 does not quantize Orange wedge payloads.
V5 does not measure serialized index overhead.
V5 does not benchmark mmap or wall-clock retrieval.

next_gate.question: Does the non-oracle Orange routing advantage survive quantized wedge storage?

supported: A layer-conditioned router trained without held-out tokens selects Orange wedges better than equivalent Pine and Random controls.
Orange wins all four folds at every tested partial-access fraction.
The non-oracle router retains most of the Orange oracle information-concentration upper bound.
Orange correlated grouping is therefore usable without direct inspection of held-out residual energy under this experimental protocol.
